title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 200 (Ratification of unauthorized act cannot injure third person)

content.overview: Section 200 provides that an act done by one person on behalf of another, without such other person’s authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect.
content.glance: An unauthorized act which, if authorized, would subject a third person to damages or terminate a third person’s right or interest cannot be made to have that effect by ratification.
content.study: An act done by one person on behalf of another, without such other person’s authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect. Current-law framing: ratification cannot be used to prejudice third persons in the specified ways.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: An act done by one person on behalf of another, without such other person’s authority, which, if done with authority, would have the effect of subjecting a third person to damages, or of terminating any right or interest of a third person, cannot, by ratification, be made to have such effect.

examples.title: No injury to third person by ratification
examples.body: An unauthorized act that would subject a third person to damages or terminate a third person’s right cannot be made effective for that purpose by ratification under Section 200.

hypotheticals.question: An unauthorized act, if authorized, would terminate a third person’s interest. Can ratification give it that effect?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 200 provides that such an act cannot, by ratification, be made to have that effect.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 200
distinctions.body: Section 200 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 200 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 200 operates only within the elements and consequences stated in its statutory text.
